_comment: P8 verify waivers for rf-de-20m. Owner authority granted at checkpoint H4 (2026-08-08, state.json human.4: 'Owner approved all 8 waiver classes'). Each entry is a HUMAN decision - gate.py load_waivers refuses any entry lacking reason/approved - and the full evidence for each is reports/verify-waivers.md, which this file is the machine-readable form of. Waived findings still appear in the gate result under 'waived': they are recorded, not erased. THE EIGHT ENTRIES BELOW COVER EXACTLY THE 31 RESIDUAL ERRORS AND NOTHING ELSE ON THE CURRENT BOARD. ===== HOW THE MATCHER LIMITS THESE, AND THE COMPENSATING CONTROL ===== gate.py:waiver_matches keys on (check|kind) + an EXACT net + a SUBSET test on refs, so a waiver that lists refs also matches a finding with EMPTY refs. That is load-bearing here: 10 of the 21 check_creepage errors are TRACK-to-TRACK (the escape tracks leaving the EPC2019 solder bars) and carry NO refs at all, so entry 1 cannot be written tightly enough to exclude a FUTURE /SW creepage error elsewhere on the board that also has empty refs. The same is true of the 12 empty-refs clearance errors among drc_routed's 48 - 22 empty-refs findings across the two gates. THE COMPENSATING CONTROL IS THAT THE RESIDUAL COUNTS ARE FIXED: check_creepage = 21 errors, gate verify = 31 errors, gate drc_routed = 55 findings. If any of those counts ever EXCEEDS its baseline, READ THE DELTA - do not assume the waiver covers it. Entries 2/3/4/5 carry no refs at all and are net-scoped, and have the same property. ===== ONE PIPELINE GOTCHA, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT SILENTLY DISARMS THIS FILE ===== gate.py resolves the default sidecar as <pcb-dir>/reports/verify-waivers.json, i.e. boards/rf-de-20m/KICAD/reports/verify-waivers.json - NOT the workspace reports/ directory this file lives in. The verify gate must therefore be run with an EXPLICIT --waivers boards/rf-de-20m/reports/verify-waivers.json, or every waiver below is silently ignored and the gate reports 31 failing.

waivers.reason: INTRA-EPC2019 DIE GEOMETRY - 21 errors, confirmed one by one. All 21 fall inside the two EPC2019 land patterns (attributed Q201 x10, Q202 x11; 10 of them are escape-track pairs and so carry empty refs) and every spacing is the die's own solder-bar pitch: 0.350 mm x15, 0.375 x2, 0.389 x2, 0.391 x2. NONE is board copper away from the die - the violation records carry item/other_item type fields and all 21 are pad-or-escape-track, ZERO involve a zone fill. The land pattern is a 0.6 mm solder-bar row, so drain-to-source gaps are 0.350 mm BY CONSTRUCTION, against IPC-2221's 0.80 mm (A6/B4) and 0.40 mm (B4/B4) at /SW's 143 V peak. IPC-2221 creepage/clearance governs BOARD conductor spacing, not the internal terminal geometry of a manufacturer-qualified component, and EPC rates this device at 200 V WITH that pitch - applying a board rule inside a qualified footprint is a category error. There is no alternative part: EPC2019 is the only 200 V GaN that closes this design and every eGaN FET in its class has comparable bar pitch, so 'choose a bigger part' has no referent. Independently proven clean elsewhere: check_creepage's own checked[].pairs[].min_gap_mm is null for every other (net, net, layer) combination it swept - including /tank/TANK_A at 180 V and the 203 V /SW-TANK_A voltage pair - across all four layers, and the /SW POUR measures 0.8004 mm to the nearest GND item, i.e. aiee_hv_143v_SW honoured to 0.4 um. Same class, same evidence and the same verdict as the APPROVED drc_routed clearance waiver (48 findings, reports/route-notes.md s13 entries 1-4). Full evidence: reports/verify-waivers.md s2 entry 1.

GEOMETRICALLY UNMEETABLE AT THE DIE - 3 errors. The two EPC2019 drain escapes (0.2500 mm each) and their rung (0.4500 mm) against an aiee_pwr_width_SW floor of 11.8942 mm. The widest connectable conductor at a 0.6 mm-pitch drain bar is 2.63 mm, so the floor cannot be met by any track; and a .kicad_dru rule BEATS a zone's local clearance during fill (measured on this board: a GND zone authored at 0.35 mm clearance filled to 0.8006 mm from every /SW pad, and three /SW fan-in lobes at 0.35 mm filled 0.0 / 0.85 / 2.08 mm2), so NO POUR of any clearance setting can reach the die either. What is in place is the pour fan-in that reference/remediations/track_width.md step 4 mandates: /SW is one 263 mm2 F.Cu island and these three are the only /SW tracks on the board besides the L301 terminal land. Identical to the approved drc_routed track_width waiver (route-notes.md s13 entry 5). Full evidence: reports/verify-waivers.md s2 entry 2.

THE CORRIDOR IS NARROWER THAN THE FLOOR - 1 error. L302's east terminal land measures 7.6510 mm against an 8.4123 mm aiee_pwr_width_tank_RFOUT floor. The corridor it crosses is 9.106 mm wide and the 0.8 mm HV clearance each side leaves 7.506 mm of legal conductor, so 8.4123 mm cannot physically exist there. The floor is also ABOVE the architecture's own binding number: kicad/constraints.json states the AC requirement is ~7.2 mm of poured copper and that the IPC-2152 DC width 'is a floor, not a pass ... wrong above ~1 MHz' - at 20 MHz the skin depth is 14.6 um and current distribution, not cross-section, governs. Identical to the approved drc_routed track_width waiver (route-notes.md s13 entry 6). Full evidence: reports/verify-waivers.md s2 entry 3.

AN ARTEFACT OF THE PER-ZONE EROSION TEST, NOT A CONDUCTOR - 1 error, reported as '+40V pour on F.Cu necks to ~4.43 mm ... needs 5.500 mm' at board-local (46.79, 7.58), i.e. the north block around L201. That block is 10-15 mm of CONTINUOUS copper; the erosion fails only because 3 of the 30 vias in the bridge's north field (local (43.8/44.7/45.6, 12.7)) sit in a 0.8 mm-deep pocket at the fill's south edge, bounded by L201's own L201_MID land. check_current.pour_neck erodes ONE zone's own fill and only where >= 2 vias of the net land, so it reports whichever rectangle happens to hold vias, at THAT rectangle's width, not the width of the conductor. Measured instead on the actual copper with a 2-D resistive-sheet solve (route/bus_solve.py: F.Cu + B.Cu rasterised at 0.25 mm, layers tied at the net's vias, the declared 7.0 A injected at J101.1 and drawn at L201.1, copper at 100 C): the north block's PEAK linear current density is 1.126 A/mm - equivalent width 6.22 mm, dT ~7.6 C - and at the three flagged vias it is 0.473 A/mm (equivalent width 14.8 mm, dT ~1.1 C). The transition itself carries 30 vias against the 14 required. The REAL +40V bottleneck, which this check could not see, was found and FIXED in the same pass (bus resistance 10.393 -> 5.508 mOhm, worst section 2.25 -> 5.29 mm equivalent width against IPC-2152's 5.500 mm). Deliberately NOT 'fixed' by deleting those three vias, which would satisfy the metric without changing any current. Full evidence: reports/verify-waivers.md s1.1 and s2 entry 4.

A MODELLING ARTEFACT OF k x TRACE_WIDTH PLUS A DESIGN DECISION - 1 error, '81.29 mm2 deficit'. The finding comes from ONE of /SW's four F.Cu tracks: L301's west terminal land, 11.894 mm WIDE and 1.200 mm LONG. check_return_path buffers the centreline by k x width = 3 x 11.894 = 35.68 mm, so a 1.2 mm stub is given a 1.2 x 71.4 mm corridor - 21.70 mm2 (27 %) of the reported deficit is NOT EVEN ON THE BOARD (the corridor runs to board-local y -18.08). The other three /SW tracks (the 0.25/0.45 mm drain escapes and their rung) produce no deficit at all. The rest of the deficit is zone B, where decisions.md D4 forbids an inner plane because a plane under a PCB air-core spiral is a SHORTED TURN; In1's plane reaches board-local x 51.00 and L301's own copperpour-not_allowed rule area starts at x 51.45, so the total copper that could ever be added is 0.45 mm of the land's 1.2 mm - and route/verify_geom.py's strict-interior test would then sit 0.05 mm from failing. THE SWITCHING LOOP ITSELF IS INTACT, measured on the actual fills: the /SW zone fill is 191.30 mm2 of which 183.90 mm2 (96.13 %) sits over continuous In1 GND, the entire remainder being one 7.41 mm2 lip along the pour's east edge; and C203, C204, C205, C206 and L202.1 are 100 % over In1. The unimaged section adds 0.24 nH (mu0.h.l/w with an image = 0.031 nH, partial self-inductance without = 0.268 nH), i.e. 0.15 % of the 164 nH inductor it feeds and 0.09 % of the 274 nH series tank, against a C_s bank that trims +/-10 %; and the current through it is the TANK current, 6.96 A rms sinusoidal at 20 MHz -> dI/dt 1.24 A/ns -> L.di/dt = 0.30 V on a node that swings 143 V pk (0.21 %). The 8 A/ns figure belongs to the drain-current transition, which flows in the FET/C_shunt/source loop. The tank's return runs on the B.Cu GND bridge and is verified still ONE island spanning the board. There is no fix; there is a design decision. Full evidence: reports/verify-waivers.md s1.2 and s2 entry 5.

THE CHECK IS HEATSINK-BLIND, CONFIRMED IN ITS SOURCE - 2 errors, 'Q20x dissipates 5.63 W into 645 mm2 of GND copper: ~288 C rise (theta_JA ~51 C/W) > 25 C allowed'. check_thermal.theta_ja() is theta_floor + (theta_0 - theta_floor).exp(-A/tau) with (140, 45, 235) for a multilayer board: COPPER AREA IS ITS ONLY INPUT. There is no heatsink, TIM or airflow term anywhere in the module, and its own docstring calls it 'a screen, not a sign-off ... +/-30 %'. This board is designed around a BOLT-ON BOTTOM-SIDE HEATSINK WITH FORCED AIR and the architecture's own path is theta_JB 3.75 + theta_BS 1.5 + theta_HS 0.7 = 5.95 C/W for the pair (decisions.md D1), giving Tj ~123 C nominal / ~142 C at the max-datasheet corner against the EPC2019's 150 C absolute maximum - and the P8 revert of the gate resistors to 4R7 recovers a further ~4 C. COMPENSATING CONTROL, AND IT IS A HARD REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE: theta_HS <= 0.7 C/W MEASURED, with forced air (OPEN-9 / HS-1). Without it a single FET reaches 175 C nominal and the pair does not close either. HS-2 (no untented vias and no through-hole pins in the bottom heatsink land) and HS-3 (THT pads clear of that land) travel with it, as does the B.Cu solder-mask aperture (HS1) that lets the sink contact bare copper. The owner's 2026-08-08 reprioritisation (25-30 V bus, 100-150 W, big fans) reduces the dissipation this covers but does NOT retire the requirement. OPEN-10 remains the real thermal uncertainty: theta_BS = 1.5 C/W for the pair is assumed, not simulated, and carries 17 C of the junction budget. Full evidence: reports/verify-waivers.md s2 entry 6.

THE CHECK IS MEASURING THE POUR, NOT THE SPIRAL - 1 error, 'L301 dissipates 10.00 W into 256 mm2 of /tank/TANK_A copper: ~769 C rise'. L301 is an ETCHED PCB AIR-CORE SPIRAL, not a placed component: its conductor is a custom-shaped SMD pad whose winding lib/geom models as the 2.8 x 8.0 mm terminal land rect, so the 256 mm2 the check measures is the tank POUR, not the winding. kicad/constraints.json says so in its own _net_note ('net added at P8 so check_thermal can run ... the authoritative thermal case for the spirals is reports/spiral-design.md, NOT this gate'). The real numbers from spiral-design.md s4: 2.57 W - not 10.0 W, which is the Q=100 planning figure, while the drawn part measures Q 388 - into 860 mm2 of plan area = 2.99 mW/mm2 against SPIRAL-1's 7 mW/mm2 rule, i.e. 2.3x clear even on the pessimistic proximity derate. The dt_c 70 in constraints is design intent; the copper runs 100-140 C, which is why TG155+ high-Tg FR4 is a MANDATORY order-time option (decisions.md D5, carried to P10). Full evidence: reports/verify-waivers.md s2 entry 7.

SAME AS THE L301 ENTRY, FOR THE SECOND SPIRAL - 1 error. L302 is an etched PCB air-core spiral whose winding is a custom SMD pad, so check_thermal sees ~1 mm2 of TANK_B pour rather than the conductor. Measured in reports/spiral-design.md s4: 2.06 W into 833 mm2 = 2.48 mW/mm2 against SPIRAL-1's 7 mW/mm2 ceiling, 2.8x clear. spiral-design.md is the authoritative thermal case for both spirals; this gate cannot be. Full evidence: reports/verify-waivers.md s2 entry 8.
